variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Set the annual rainfall a source associates with a crop beside the annual rainfall totals in the NASA record.
variable_mappings.temporal_basis: Monthly totals added up to calendar-year totals, one per year on record.
limitations: An annual total hides how rain is split between seasons; the pilot site has two rainy seasons a year.
Rainfall is not the water available to a crop: runoff, evaporation from bare soil, soil storage and irrigation all intervene.
The NASA rainfall is a reanalysis estimate for a grid cell tens of kilometres wide, not a gauge on the farm.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Combine the share of soil water a crop can use before stress with how much water the soil holds.
variable_mappings.temporal_basis: Static soil properties for the rooting zone.
limitations: Soil water characteristics must come from the user or a soil source. Reference values by texture class are typical values, not measurements.
The published fraction assumes an evapotranspiration rate of about 5 mm/day.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Set a crop's documented growing period beside the length of a rainy season in the NASA daily record.
variable_mappings.temporal_basis: Daily rainfall within a season whose start and end are defined by a cited rule.
limitations: No rule for the start and end of a rainy season has been adopted yet. Phase A4 must define and cite one.
Published growing periods are indicative and depend on the variety.
A crop can finish on stored soil water after the rains end, so season length is not a strict limit.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Multiply by reference evapotranspiration to estimate potential crop water use late in the season.
limitations: Reference evapotranspiration is not retrieved; it must be calculated, and the standard method needs wind speed, which the data layer does not yet retrieve.
Crop coefficients are for well-watered crops under standard conditions and overstate the water use of a stressed rain-fed crop.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Multiply by reference evapotranspiration to estimate potential crop water use early in the season.
limitations: Reference evapotranspiration is not retrieved; it must be calculated, and the standard method needs wind speed, which the data layer does not yet retrieve.
The source calls initial-stage coefficients 'only approximations' that depend on how often the soil is wetted.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Multiply by reference evapotranspiration to estimate potential crop water use at mid-season.
limitations: Reference evapotranspiration is not retrieved; it must be calculated, and the standard method needs wind speed, which the data layer does not yet retrieve.
Crop coefficients are for well-watered crops in a sub-humid climate; the source requires adjustment for other climates.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Combine rooting depth with how much water the soil holds per unit depth to estimate the water a crop can draw on.
variable_mappings.temporal_basis: Static soil properties for the rooting zone.
limitations: Soil water characteristics must come from the user or a soil source; they are never taken from NASA weather data.
Published rooting depths assume no restricting soil layer; soil depth at the site is unknown.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Set a crop's indicative seasonal water use beside the rainfall of a past season, as a first indication of water shortfall or surplus.
variable_mappings.temporal_basis: Rainfall totalled over a defined growing season, one value per season on record.
limitations: The crop figure is evapotranspiration, not rainfall demand. The two are not directly comparable without a water balance.
Rainfall is not the water available to a crop: runoff, soil storage, deep drainage and irrigation all intervene.
Indicative water needs are held for maize, sorghum and common bean only.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Set the soil pH a source associates with a crop beside the pH of the field.
limitations: Soil pH must be measured or supplied by the user. It is never inferred from NASA temperature or rainfall.
The published ranges mix optimal, preferred and tolerated values, which must not be treated alike.
No pH range is held for cowpea.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Set the temperatures a source associates with a crop beside the NASA record for the growing season.
variable_mappings.temporal_basis: Daily values within the growing season. Monthly means may be used only for a general picture.
limitations: A monthly or seasonal mean cannot show short spells of heat or cold, which are what damage crops.
Sources rarely say whether they mean a daily mean, a day-time or a seasonal temperature, so a like-for-like comparison is often not possible.
NASA temperatures are for a grid cell at its average elevation; the pilot cell averages 1,328 m.
A crop's temperature preference says nothing about disease incidence or yield.

variable_mappings.comparison_intent: Indicate which crops are relatively more sensitive to a seasonal water deficit.
limitations: Needs a calculated water deficit, which does not exist yet.
The factor describes relative yield loss. This project does not predict yields, so it may be used only to compare sensitivity between crops.
Held for maize, sorghum and beans only.
